newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks retreat, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks retreat, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: U.S. shares retreated on Thursday, extending losses amid profit-taking and weakness in the technology sector.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which powered higher the past two days after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave an upbeat testimony on the U.S. economy, paused.
It shed around 66 points, or 0.81 percent, to 8022, as the New York Stock Exchange set curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
Technology stocks also slipped, with the Nasdaq composite losing around 13 points to 1555. Market heavyweight Microsoft Corp lost 5-6/16 to 136-1/16.
